items.text: Price criterion uses a discounted year-1 price; renewal list price $303k with up to 8% increases plus a $95k implementation fee make Tallis the most expensive over 3 years
paraphrases: Pricing is scored on a teaser: the 40% first-year discount hides a $303k renewal plus up to 8% yearly increases.
Total cost of ownership over 3 years makes Tallis the most expensive once the $95k implementation fee is added.
Cheapest only in year 1 - from year 2 the list price jumps to $303k.

items.text: Tallis cannot handle the union shift-differential and overtime-averaging rules (only 'on the roadmap'), while the other two configured them in the sandbox
paraphrases: Tallis can't do our union shift-differential rules yet - it's only on the Q3 roadmap.
Overtime-averaging rules for the unionized sites were configured by Corvane and Meridew in a sandbox, not by Tallis.
A core requirement (union pay rules) is unmet; the features score ignores it.

items.text: Tallis references are small, single-site, non-union customers; nothing shows it works at 1,400 employees across 9 sites with unions
paraphrases: All three Tallis references are tiny single-site non-union firms (60-190 staff) - not comparable to us.
Reference customers don't prove it scales to 1,400 employees on 9 sites.
References are not representative of our size or union complexity.

items.text: Features were scored by one person from vendor-scripted demos; the payroll team that will use the system never saw them
paraphrases: Scores come from vendor-scripted demos judged by a single evaluator, not from our own scenarios.
The 6-person payroll team who will run it daily hasn't seen any demo.
No end users or stakeholders were involved in scoring features or ease of use.

items.text: Uptime figures are marketing claims; Tallis offers no uptime SLA while the others contract 99.9% with credits
paraphrases: The 99.99% uptime is from Tallis's marketing page; its contract has no SLA at all.
Availability claims are self-reported - only Corvane and Meridew back theirs with service credits.
'Commercially reasonable efforts' is not an uptime commitment.

items.text: Lock-in: proprietary data export and a 6-month termination fee make leaving Tallis expensive
paraphrases: Vendor lock-in: history exports only in Tallis's proprietary format.
A termination fee of 6 months' fees makes exit costly.
Data portability and exit costs are ignored.

items.text: Vendor viability: a 3-year-old 40-person startup mid-fundraise is a risk for mission-critical payroll
paraphrases: Vendor viability risk: Tallis is a 3-year-old, 40-employee startup still raising its next round.
If Tallis goes out of business, our payroll is stranded - the others are 15+ years old and profitable.
Financial stability of the vendor isn't weighed for a mission-critical system.

items.text: Scoring arithmetic: the weights add up to 110%, not 100%
paraphrases: The criterion weights sum to 110%, so the weighted totals are on an inconsistent scale.
Weights add to more than 100% (30+25+20+15+10+10).
Weighting error: percentages don't sum to 100, so totals need to be normalized.
negatives: The weighting puts too much emphasis on features.

items.text: Artificial urgency: the expiring year-1 price pressures a rushed decision on a system needed in 11 months
paraphrases: The 'price expires Friday' deadline is a sales pressure tactic; we have 11 months.
Rushing to sign this week to lock in a discount ignores that the discount is the problem.
Artificial urgency from the expiring offer.

decoys.text: Security / compliance certification of the vendors was not checked
decoys.why_not: All three provided SOC 2 Type II reports, reviewed by IT Security with no exceptions.
paraphrases: No security review of the vendors.
Should verify SOC 2 / security certifications before signing.
Information security posture of the vendor isn't assessed.

decoys.text: Integration with the ERP was not verified
decoys.why_not: IT confirmed prebuilt ERP connectors and tested a sample payroll journal export for all three.
paraphrases: ERP integration risk is not addressed.
Need to test the connector to our ERP / accounting system.
Integration with existing systems not validated.

decoys.text: Vendor support levels / hours were not compared
decoys.why_not: All three offer 24/7 phone support with a 1-hour response commitment written into the draft contracts.
paraphrases: Support coverage and response times are not compared across vendors.
What happens when payroll breaks at 2am - is there phone support?
No evaluation of vendor customer support quality.
